unit.name: Collecting initial wake-word data
unit.description: This segment covers how to obtain a first training set for a custom trigger phrase when no public dataset exists, emphasizing consent-driven collection of real data and a cautious stance toward early synthetic data generation.
unit.summary: After the literature search, the bottleneck becomes data: there is no internet-scale dataset of people saying the custom phrase "Robert, turn on," so the team must collect examples itself [ts=1088s] [ts=1136s]. The instructor endorses walking around, clearly asking for permission, and recording willing participants because real data is fast to gather and removes uncertainty about realism [ts=1177s] [ts=1264s]. He treats text-to-speech and other synthetic generation as useful but not first-choice, because they introduce extra knobs such as voice diversity and distribution mismatch that can slow early progress [ts=1322s] [ts=1372s]. A self-driving car analogy reinforces the point: synthetic worlds often look sufficient to humans while still missing the diversity required by a model [ts=1445s] [ts=1500s].

key_points.text: Custom wake-word projects often require collecting a phrase-specific dataset because no public dataset matches the exact trigger phrase.
Collect real recordings with explicit permission before relying on synthetic speech generation.
Synthetic data is useful but can introduce hidden hyperparameters such as limited voice diversity.
Real data removes one major uncertainty because it already reflects the natural target distribution.

kp_catalog.name: Collect real data with explicit user consent
kp_catalog.description: A data-collection principle that favors natural examples gathered transparently and with permission when bootstrapping a system.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: The lecture explicitly centers permission, privacy, and real recordings as the fastest reliable way to bootstrap the trigger dataset [ts=1264s] [ts=1320s].

kp_catalog.name: Synthetic-versus-real data trade-off
kp_catalog.description: The idea that synthetic data can be powerful but adds realism and diversity risks that often make real data preferable early on.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: Synthetic-vs-real data is a concrete data strategy tradeoff, not a standalone gateway.
